finding.claim: POST /profile/avatar fetches an attacker-supplied URL server-side with axios; the only check is a https:// prefix, with no host allowlist, IP/CIDR blocking, or redirect re-validation. Response body is not returned; only its byte length is. Severity MEDIUM (blind SSRF with length oracle).

trace.note: only check: typeof string and startsWith("https://"); scheme-only, does not close
axios.get(url) dispatches request to attacker-chosen host; axios follows redirects by default so https:// URL can redirect to http://169.254.169.254 or RFC-1918 hosts
res.json({ bytes: img.data.length }) returns only the response size

finding.guards_checked: Type check (string) passes any string; scheme prefix check does not restrict host; no host allowlist; no IP/CIDR or private-range blocking; no maxRedirects:0 or per-hop re-validation; route is unauthenticated. Redirect-to-http bypass of the https check believed possible via follow-redirects but not executed/verified.

verdict.guard_found: none. server.js:11 is a scheme-only check (typeof string plus startsWith("https://")), which the criteria say does not close the finding. No host allowlist, IP/CIDR blocking, or maxRedirects:0 appears anywhere in server.js, and the route has no auth middleware (server.js:9).
verdict.reason: The sink at server.js:14 (axios.get(url)) takes req.body.avatarUrl (server.js:10) from an unauthenticated POST, and the only check at server.js:11 is the https:// prefix, so an attacker can point the request at any HTTPS host, including one that redirects to internal addresses. Every trace line (10, 11, 14, 15) matches the candidate's description.

finding.claim: GET /users/:id: host is hardcoded (USER_SVC = http://users.internal:8080); user input only reaches the path via encodeURIComponent, which encodes @, /, ?, #. Path traversal within the host at most, not SSRF. Closed.

trace.note: user value occupies path only; host and scheme fixed

finding.guards_checked: encodeURIComponent blocks host injection via @ and path-separator escape via /; hardcoded host and scheme; '..' not encoded so path traversal within users.internal is possible but is not SSRF.

verdict.guard_found: server.js:19 encodeURIComponent(req.params.id) keeps the user value in one path segment. Host and scheme are fixed by the constant USER_SVC at server.js:7, so the attacker cannot choose the destination host.
verdict.reason: All three trace lines are accurate (server.js:7, 19, 20), and req.params.id at server.js:18 is attacker-controlled, but the value only reaches the URL path because the host and scheme come from the hardcoded USER_SVC at server.js:7, so there is no SSRF. The only residual is that an id of ".." yields a dot-segment resolving to /v1/ on the same internal host (server.js:19-20), which is not SSRF and not a finding under the criteria.
